extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers and general creative writers seeking craft guidance
extracted.subtask_description: A distilled set of 20 practical rules and additional craft principles (from Stephen King's On Writing) for aspiring fiction writers covering voice, discipline, revision, description, and habits that support sustained writing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize yourself first
rubrics_metrics.description: Write for personal satisfaction first; tell yourself the story initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewriting focuses on removing non-essential elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid passive voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on passive verbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Timid writers like passive verbs for the same reason that timid lovers like passive partners. The passive voice is safe." Use active constructions to produce stronger, clearer prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize adverbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use adverbs sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The adverb is not your friend." Prefer strong verbs and precise nouns over adverbial modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skip adverbs after dialogue tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid adverbs following 'he said' and 'she said'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially after dialogue tags; let the dialogue and context show tone or manner rather than tagging with adverbs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't obsess over grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not let perfect syntax get in the way of storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on welcoming readers and telling engaging stories over perfect grammar; mechanics matter but should not paralyze the creative process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust your instincts / banish fear
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on your instincts and avoid writing driven by fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "I'm convinced that fear is at the root of most bad writing." Banish self-doubt that leads to timid choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read extensively
rubrics_metrics.description: Read a lot as an essential component of becoming a writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "If you don't have time to read, you don't have the time (or the tools) to write." Reading supplies models, vocabulary, and craft lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write truthfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for authenticity in expression rather than trying to please others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic voice and truthful depiction of characters and situations are prioritized over pandering or fashionable choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate TV / distractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove television and other major distractions from your life as an aspiring writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "TV…really is about the last thing an aspiring writer needs." Consciously reduce attention-sapping activities to free time and mental energy for writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Set and keep a deadline for completing first drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete first drafts within three months — the length of a season — to maintain momentum and avoid endless tinkering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain personal wellness
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain physical health and stable relationships to support writing productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good health and supportive relationships help sustain the discipline and energy required for writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work incrementally
rubrics_metrics.description: Accomplish writing one word at a time; steady incremental work wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The work is always accomplished one word at a time." Emphasizes small, consistent progress over waiting for inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a focused environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange a writing space free of phones, screens, and games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove immediate digital distractions from your writing environment to foster concentration and flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop your own voice / style
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid imitating other writers; cultivate an individual voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't imitate other writers; rely on your own sensibility and perspectives to develop distinctive style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excavate stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat stories as pre-existing relics to be uncovered rather than fully plotted inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Stories are relics, part of an undiscovered pre-existing world." Favor intuition and discovery over rigid plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Take extended breaks (e.g., six weeks) before revising to gain perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six-week layoffs before revision provide fresh perspective and make it easier to spot problems and necessary cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit ruthlessly / kill your darlings
rubrics_metrics.description: Be willing to cut cherished lines, scenes, or elements that don't serve the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Kill your darlings, kill your darlings…even when it breaks your egocentric little scribbler's heart." Revision should eliminate what is non-essential or self-indulgent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background research appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Do research but keep it unobtrusive and mostly in backstory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep research from overwhelming the narrative; use it to inform authenticity without bogging down the story with exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn through practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve by reading and writing extensively; practice is the primary teacher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading and sustained writing practice are the 'schoolmasters' of craft — formal rules are secondary to doing the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace creative joy
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach writing as an intrinsically rewarding, even 'magical' activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Writing is magic." Pursue intrinsic fulfillment rather than external validation alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description (selective detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good description uses a few well-chosen details that stand for everything else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "A good description usually consists of a few well chosen details that will stand for everything else. Description should begin in the writer's imagination, but should finish in the readers." Avoid exhaustive listing; let details evoke larger scenes or emotions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot vs Story (prefer discovery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer intuition and discovery over heavy plotting; real life is often 'plotless.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: King distrusts plot — "our lives are largely plotless" — and recommends leaning on intuition/discovery rather than forcing contrived plot structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening line
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft an opening line that invites the reader to begin the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening line should draw the reader in; it's an invitation rather than a full summary or explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision formula: 2nd Draft = 1st Draft – 10%
rubrics_metrics.description: King's suggested revision rule: reduce the first draft by about 10% for the second draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a heuristic to tighten prose and eliminate excess; it's a concrete guideline for ruthless editing.
